verdict.justification: Both plans cover all required SKUs, select the correct senior eligible crews, meet the daily capacity and changeover requirements, and flag the conflicting polymer figures in the BOM. B is preferable because its production, material, and summary calculations are formula-driven, whereas A hard-codes results and prematurely rounds some run times, such as 34.29 minutes for G6ABS. B also links daily totals directly to explicit production-day assignments, making the schedule easier to audit and revise. Its labor summary clearly uses "Total Minutes," resolving the template’s conflicting hours/minutes labels, while A reports rounded decimal hours despite the section requesting whole minutes. B supplies a useful manager email draft and transparently states that it was not actually sent. B does make an unnecessary departure from the yellow-cell-only instruction by adding columns L and M, but its stronger calculation traceability and handoff outweigh that drawback.

decisive_issues.issue: Run-time inputs are hard-coded and prematurely rounded rather than retaining full precision.
Formula-driven run-time calculations retain precision and respond to demand changes.
Provides an actionable manager handoff while accurately disclosing that email was not sent.
decisive_issues.quote: The plan was not emailed. No plant manager address was provided and no send capability was available here; see Email to Plant Manager.txt.

decisive_issues.issue: Adds cells outside the requested yellow input area, a minor instruction-following weakness.
decisive_issues.quote: Columns L and M (Production Day, Run Sequence) were added to the plan to show the schedule that drives the daily totals; they are not part of the original yellow area.
